title: Source-of-truth and package-boundary matrix
affectedPackages: Identity Directory for Organization and Person
versioning: contracts/authority/matrix.json and this record share one revision counter, so a row is cited as DR-0002@<revision>:<row-id>. A change to a row's command owner, target authority, privacy floor or visibility, scope, or package is breaking and gives the row the new revision; filling a pending cell or adding a row is additive. The check compares matrix.json with the base branch (AUTH_REVISION_NOT_BUMPED, AUTH_COMPATIBILITY_UNDECLARED, AUTH_ROW_REMOVED). A ratified revision pins the SHA-256 of matrix.json, packages.json, and owner-labels.json, so an unapproved edit fails DR_APPROVAL_STALE.
supersession: A ratified revision is never edited. A changed decision gets a new revision that names the prior one in supersedes (DR-0002@<n>) and gives supersessionReason; citers of changed breaking rows re-cite, and #17's LEAF_GATE_SUPERSEDED flags stale citations. An unratified revision can be reverted.
context: Issue #16 (ROUNDS-01-L02). Spec lines refer to rounds-review docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-rounds-review-board-design.md; code citations are lines at 62d4eae.

securityConsequences.account: No runtime or privilege change. Every account-scoped row inherits the server-derived account scope (#9, ROUNDS-00B-L01); #172 (ROUNDS-34-L03) registers each row's authorization.
securityConsequences.privacy: Each account row names a privacy floor from spec 2142-2148; #72 (ROUNDS-14-L01) may only tighten it. Secret rows (sessions, provider credentials, share bearer digests) have only verifier or gateway consumers.
securityConsequences.secret: Secrets appear by name and location only (AI_KEY_SECRET, PB_ADMIN_PASSWORD, resume_share_links.token, pocketbase_auth). The demo row cites its quota fields (1700000600_demo_user.js:15-17), never its credential lines. The check fails a citation of a credential line, any credential value the audited revision assigns, and secret-shaped strings in these files.
securityConsequences.publicBoundary: Every row lists a public-share entry: the consumer, or n/a with the reason. Career Profile, Directory, and Artifact rows reach a public capability only through a frozen Share Projection (#93), Legacy Artifact Snapshots only through a contained capability (#11), and share capability metadata only through the public renderer. Secret rows and the server-only Test Definition, Harness Revision, and Artifact Renderer Contract rows have only verifier or gateway consumers.

decisions.title: One row per durable concept and relation
decisions.decision: The 31 spec rows (spec 781-811) keep their five columns verbatim, and every row adds: id, revision, compatibility, scope (account, platform-global, or pack-owned), a #15 term, a command owner (one spec service and the owning leaf), commands, baseline writers at 62d4eae, exactly one target authority, storage (pending #18), a privacy floor (account rows) or visibility (platform and pack rows), a ledger disposition, transfer and projection blocks, typed consumers, a package, and the nine registration columns. A cell holds a value, pending:<leaf-id>, n/a:<reason>, or blocked:OD-<n>. Rows with pending cells are citable and closed to implementation until the leaf fills them; blocked rows are not citable.

alternatives.reason: Leaves already disagree; nothing machine-checkable would stop a second writer.
Collections are #155's stores; several mix concepts (applications holds Opportunity and Pursuit).

decisions.consequences: Implementers find a concept's single writer, read models, privacy floor, package, and retirement in one place and cite it as DR-0002@<revision>:<row-id>.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Baseline writers sit apart from the one target authority
decisions.decision: baseline_writers lists the modules and lines that write each store at 62d4eae; target_authority names the one writable authority the row moves to. More than one writer module for a store, or a derived consumer that writes its source, needs a conflict ID with a disposition and resolving leaf. A registry defined in code names its store bundled:<registry>, so copies of one registry in several modules count as several writers. A row has one writable authority at any revision: the legacy writer until its transfer leaf switches it, then the target. Compatibility adapters read, shadow, or compare, and never write.

alternatives.option: Reject any row with two writers
alternatives.reason: Every conflicted baseline row (C1 to C16) would fail, so the matrix could not describe today.

decisions.consequences: Rule 2 fails an unflagged second writer; rule 1 fails a second target authority.
decisions.migrationImpact: Each conflict names the leaf that resolves it; nothing moves here.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Baseline conflicts C1 to C17
decisions.decision: C1 to C13 are flagged as the issue lists them. Building the matrix found four more second writers at 62d4eae, flagged as C14 (the SPA and the runner both write ai_settings), C15 (both create and delete resume_share_links), C16 (the demo reset deletes nine collections' rows from the client), and C17 (four modules each define their own copy of the pursuit stage list), each with its disposition and resolving leaf.

alternatives.reason: Rule 2 would fail, or the matrix would hide a second writer.

decisions.consequences: Each resolving leaf removes its conflict's second writer. The conflicts stay listed as facts about 62d4eae, and the check requires C1 to C13 while the matrix audits that revision.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Spec rows that split

alternatives.reason: A row has one command owner, and these concepts have two or three.

decisions.consequences: Each part carries its own owner, privacy floor, and consumers.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Rows beyond the issue's list
decisions.decision: Durable concepts the issue's list does not name get rows too, so every leaf's owner sentence names a row: execution admission (#1) and execution attempts (#3), Capture Items (#50), Processing Attempts (#54), typed relations (#37), evidence gap maps (#139), Today item state (#144), ATS analysis (#86), resume autosave drafts (#83), export and restore (#91, #92), view state (browser sort, filter, width, and focus keys, #158), and status registries (#48).

alternatives.reason: Rule 9 would fail every browser key family that is view state, and several owner sentences would name no row.

decisions.consequences: Every baseline store has a row, and each owner sentence names its rows or says the leaf owns none.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Storage, projections, and privacy are enforced elsewhere
decisions.decision: storage is pending:ROUNDS-02-L01 until #18 assigns a store. Projection blocks name sources, watermark, stale and degraded behavior, and one projector, and every source lists the read model as a consumer; #23 (ROUNDS-02-L06) and #146 (ROUNDS-31-L01) enforce them at runtime. Privacy floors use the five spec class names; #72 (ROUNDS-14-L01) owns class definitions, sink policy, and the field map, which may only tighten a floor, and loosening one needs a breaking revision.

alternatives.reason: #72 owns them; two copies would drift.

decisions.consequences: Filling storage or the registration columns is additive, so citations hold.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Boundary with #155
decisions.decision: This matrix owns concept-level rows and dispositions. baseline-stores.json lists every collection and browser key family at 62d4eae with its rows; #155 (ROUNDS-32-L01) seeds its store registry from it, maps every store, field, and key to a row, and repoints rule 9 at that registry.

alternatives.reason: #155 owns the field-level inventory; this leaf stays at concept level.

decisions.consequences: A store with no row fails rule 9 until #155 takes the check over.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.

decisions.title: Owner labels map to services
decisions.decision: owner-labels.json maps each of the 36 catalog owner labels to one spec service, none (UI, composition, and program labels own no commands), blocked:OD-1 (AI Trust Platform), or per-row. Six labels take per-row services: Portability and Sharing, Read Platform, Identity and Career Profile; Identity, Authorization, and Sharing; Domain Platform; and Relationships and Networking. A row whose command owner is a leaf of a capability must take that label's service for it.

alternatives.reason: Six labels own rows in different services.

decisions.consequences: owner-sentence-corrections.json rewrites the 101 templated owner sentences to name rows and the owning leaf, for #17's re-authorization.
decisions.migrationImpact: No issue body is edited here.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Row compatibility and revisions
decisions.decision: The matrix revision equals DR-0002's. Each changed row declares compatibility. A change to a row's command owner, target authority, privacy floor or visibility, scope, or package is breaking: the row takes the new matrix revision, so only that row's citers re-cite. Filling a pending cell or adding a row is additive. Rows are superseded, never deleted.

alternatives.option: One compatibility flag for the whole matrix
alternatives.reason: One breaking row would reblock every citer.

decisions.consequences: The check compares matrix.json with the base branch.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Export gate at ROUNDS-01 closure
decisions.decision: The universal gate of spec 3194-3219 (database and transaction ADR, ERD, command schemas, authorization matrix, Audit Entry and Domain Event catalogue, and the rest of that list) is a ROUNDS-01 closure gate, as DR-0001 correction C1 recorded. Its producers are #17 to #22 (ROUNDS-01-L03, ROUNDS-02-L01 to L05), #172 (ROUNDS-34-L03), and each contract leaf. This leaf creates part of that gate, so it is not blocked by it (spec 3232-3236): it merges on #15 (ROUNDS-01-L01), its only prerequisite, and its rollout gate opens once #15 is complete, current, and verified.

alternatives.option: Gate this merge on the export gate
alternatives.reason: The gate needs #18, which depends on this leaf, so it could never open.

decisions.consequences: Rollout: ratify matrix revision 1 with conformance green on main, then unblock only the leaves whose prerequisites include ROUNDS-01-L02.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Service for provider invocation
decisions.decision: Open. Spec 808 names a "Provider gateway", which is not one of the 17 services, and the issue proposes no default. AI Trust Platform rows (AI provider credential, AI role settings, Generation Proposal, Staged Provider Result, Provider Invocation Receipt) name their leaf and carry service blocked:OD-1; #73 (ROUNDS-14-L02) keeps the keyring.

alternatives.reason: The approved spec lists 17; adding one is the owner's call.

alternatives.option: One of the 17 (Account Service holds the secret store, spec 808)
alternatives.reason: Splits the gateway from its receipts; also the owner's call.

decisions.consequences: The five rows are not citable until the owner decides.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Deciding is additive for other rows.

decisions.title: Career Activity has one owner
decisions.decision: Settled by the approved direction: PRODUCT.md lines 67-70 make Career Activity the sole mutable authority for scheduled and completed interviews, conversations, follow-ups, submissions, milestones, and other dated occurrences. #107 (ROUNDS-22-L02) owns the aggregate in the Interview Process Service; #112 (ROUNDS-23-L02, conversations) and #88 (ROUNDS-17-L04, submissions) register kinds and call its commands.
decisions.consequences: The Career Activity rows are citable; #103, #106, #112, #113, and #116 unblock on this point.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one with a new revision.

decisions.title: Projector for the Preparation plan read model
decisions.decision: Default taken from the issue: #152 (ROUNDS-31-L07), filed as a second Today read model, is retargeted to the Preparation plan read model (spec 1977), so each of the nine read models has one projector. #143 (ROUNDS-30-L02) keeps Today.

alternatives.reason: Two Today projectors and none for the Preparation plan.

decisions.consequences: The Preparation plan row names #152 as projector.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: The owner can move the projector in a superseding revision.

decisions.title: Pack activation scope
decisions.decision: Default taken: spec 809 allows "Account or deployment Pack Activation", and #40's approved scope is "activate per account", so the Pack Activation row is account-scoped: the deployment installs a pack once, and each account enables it, on by default for first-party packs.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. No stored data changes; each row's transfer leaf moves its data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: A superseding revision can make activation deployment-only.

od.default: per-account enablement over a deployment installation

decisions.title: Login streak
decisions.decision: Open. #24 asks whether the login streak stays, moves to Account, or retires. Until the owner decides it stays a browser cache (rounds.loginStreak.v1, with and without the user id) that #158 (ROUNDS-32-L04) keeps and exports; its row is blocked:OD-5.

alternatives.option: Move it to an Account preference

decisions.consequences: The login streak row is not citable until the owner decides.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Deciding is additive for other rows.
